children: South Korea's goverment has dropped a plan to tighten tax rules on non-resident homeowners about a month after proposing it, following public criticism.
The basic comprehensive real estate holding tax deduction for single-home owners will remain at 1.2 billion won ($870,000), abandoning a proposal to trim the tax benefit to 900 million won.
The final tax revision package was approved during a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.

On August 3, South Korea proposed property tax changes aimed at imposing higher duties on wealthy homeowners by cutting tax deductions for property investors, as part of policy efforts to stabilise a hot housing market.
